title: Spike: credentialsd provider API and portal on KDE Plasma
body:
## Question

Can a third-party credential provider register with credentialsd (v0.3.x, pre-release) and serve a WebAuthn create/get request that arrives through xdg-desktop-portal on KDE Plasma?

## Why it matters

The whole design is an integration layer on credentialsd (constraint C1). If the provider API or the KDE portal path does not exist, the TPM provider and the KeePassXC bridge have nowhere to plug in.

**Blocks:** TPM credential provider, KeePassXC provider bridge, routing policy.

## Method

Read the credentialsd provider interface and portal code at the tagged release; build it with the patched xdg-desktop-portal; register a stub provider that logs requests; drive one request from a test client.

Mark each command and script tested or untested, with versions and hardware class.

## Time box

Proposed: 2 working days. Stop at the time box and record what is known.

## Done when

- [ ] A spike note exists in `docs/spikes/` (from `docs/templates/spike.md`) with question, method, evidence and a Yes / No / Partly answer.
- [ ] Every claim cites upstream source, docs or a reproducible run at a named version.
- [ ] The architecture note, `workspace.dsl` or an ADR is updated if the answer changes the design.

title: Spike: PAM module publishes method state over the Agent's D-Bus API
body:
## Question

Can `pam_linuxhello` run face, fingerprint and PIN in parallel and publish their state on the Agent's D-Bus API from inside a PAM conversation (greeter, lock screen, sudo)?

## Why it matters

PAM is text-only (UX design consequence). If the PAM module cannot hold a D-Bus connection cleanly in every PAM context, the PAM module and the Agent boundary moves (ADR-0001 expects this possibility).

**Blocks:** Unified prompt (UX2), parallel methods (UX1), the PAM container boundary.

## Method

Prototype a PAM module that opens a system or session bus connection in each context (sddm/greeter, kscreenlocker, sudo, login on a TTY) and emits a signal; record which contexts allow it and under which AppArmor profile.

Mark each command and script tested or untested, with versions and hardware class.

## Time box

Proposed: 2 working days. Stop at the time box and record what is known.

title: Threat model and first security properties
body:
Write the threat model in `docs/security/`: assets, actors, trust boundaries, entry points and threats, using the target architecture's threat list as the starting point. Derive the first security properties from it, each in plain language with the name of its future test (for example `caller_from_other_origin_is_refused`). Tests that cannot run yet start as `#[ignore]` placeholders named after the property.

Owner: the maintainer (GOVERNANCE.md). Tests are written with AI assistance and reviewed by behaviour.

title: Path-filtered CI with one aggregate required check
body:
Guardrail 3 (ADR-0001): CI filtered by path, one job per crate. Deferred until the crates hold real code, because a required check whose workflow a path filter skips stays pending and blocks the merge. Needs one aggregate required check that always reports.

## Done when

- [ ] Per-crate jobs run only when that crate or a shared file changes.
- [ ] One always-reporting required check gates the merge; the ruleset is updated in the same change.

title: Fuzz every parser in CI
body:
Every parser (policy files first) gets a fuzz target and a time-boxed fuzz run in CI. Blocked until the policy parser exists.

## Done when

- [ ] `cargo fuzz` targets for each parser.
- [ ] A required CI job runs them for a fixed time on every pull request that touches a parser.

title: Decide the 1.0 browser fallback: KeePassXC-Browser or the credentialsd extension
body:
Spike 0006 found that no stock browser calls the credentials portal, so 1.0 needs a browser fallback. Two candidates:

- **KeePassXC-Browser**: released, works on any site, but software keys unlocked by the KeePassXC database, and no TPM custody.
- **credentialsd web extension**: reaches credentialsd today, but limited to two demo sites and passes the origin from the page side (spike 0006, evidence 5).

## Done when

- [ ] The origin-trust question is answered: can a native-messaging helper establish the origin, or must it come from the browser?
- [ ] An ADR records the fallback for 1.0 and its retirement condition (stock browser portal support).

title: Policy 1/4: schema types and strict parsing of one policy file
body:
Starts once the policy semantics PR (`docs/architecture/policy-semantics.md`) is on `main`.

## Implementation brief

**Goal:** `parse_layer(text: &str) -> Result<Layer, PolicyError>` turns one policy file into typed values and rejects anything outside the schema.

**Files:**
1. `crates/linuxhello-agent/Cargo.toml`: add `serde = { version = "1.0.229", features = ["derive"] }` and `toml = "1.1.8"`.
2. `crates/linuxhello-agent/src/lib.rs` (new): `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, crate doc comment, `pub mod policy;`.
3. `crates/linuxhello-agent/src/policy/mod.rs` (new): `pub mod schema;` and re-exports.
4. `crates/linuxhello-agent/src/policy/schema.rs` (new): types, validation, `parse_layer`, tests.

**Schema** (every table and key optional; `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` on every struct):

| Table | Key | Type and range |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `[pin]` | `min_length` | integer 4–64 |
| | `max_length` | integer 4–127 |
| | `digits`, `lowercase`, `uppercase`, `special` | `"required"`, `"allowed"`, `"disallowed"` |
| | `history` | integer 0–50 |
| | `expiry_days` | integer 1–730 |
| | `lockout_attempts` | integer 1–32 |
| | `lockout_minutes` | integer 1–1440 |
| `[methods]` | `biometrics_allowed`, `face_requires_ir`, `require_hardware_tpm` | boolean |
| `[context.<name>]` | name | `login`, `unlock`, `sudo`, `session` only |
| | `methods` | non-empty array of `"pin"`, `"fingerprint"`, `"face"`, no duplicates |
| | `factors` | integer 1–2 |
| | `reverify_after` | integer + `s`/`m`/`h`/`d`, between 1 s and 30 d; parse to `std::time::Duration` |
| `[rp_class.<name>]` | name | 1–64 chars of `[a-z0-9_-]` |
| | `match` | non-empty array of patterns |
| | `provider` | `"tpm"`, `"keepassxc"`, `"any"` |
| | `prompt` | `"none"`, `"presence"`, `"reverify"` |
| | `factors` | integer 1–2 |
| | `require_second_credential` | boolean |

A pattern is an exact domain (`bank.example`) or `*.` + domain (`*.bank.example`). Store it lower-cased without a trailing dot. Reject `*` alone, `*` anywhere else, empty labels, and characters outside `[a-z0-9.-]` after lower-casing.

**Tests first** (in `schema.rs`, each must fail before the code exists):
- `unknown_key_makes_file_unparseable` (e.g. `min_lenght`, an unknown table, an unknown context name)
- `out_of_range_value_makes_file_unparseable` (one case per ranged key, both ends)
- `invalid_rp_pattern_makes_file_unparseable` (`*`, `bank.*.example`, `*.`, `a..b`, `exa mple.com`)
- `duplicate_method_makes_file_unparseable`
- `reverify_after_parses_units` (`90s`, `15m`, `8h`, `30d`; rejects `0s`, `31d`, `8`, `8x`)
- `example_policy_parses`: `include_str!("../../../../policy/policy.example.toml")` parses
- `empty_file_is_an_empty_layer`

**Constraints:**
- Invariant 3, fail closed: "Unparseable policy denies everything except the PIN. No fallback silently weakens authentication."
- Invariant 4: no `unsafe`. The crate root keeps `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.
- Invariant 8: no host names, home paths or machine details in code, tests or commits.
- Dependencies: only those named in this brief. No `unwrap()`/`expect()` outside tests.

**Acceptance:**
```sh
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
cargo deny check
bash scripts/ci/unsafe-policy.sh
```

**Out of scope:** merging layers, defaults, reading files from disk, any query API. Do not touch `main.rs`, other crates, CI or docs.

title: Policy 2/4: built-in defaults and layer merging
body:
Depends on Policy 1/4.

## Implementation brief

**Goal:** `merge(admin: &[Layer], user: Option<&Layer>) -> Result<Effective, Contradiction>` produces the effective policy with a `managed` flag per key, following the layering rules below.

**Files:**
1. `crates/linuxhello-agent/src/policy/defaults.rs` (new): the built-in defaults.
2. `crates/linuxhello-agent/src/policy/merge.rs` (new): restrictiveness, merging, invariants, tests.
3. `crates/linuxhello-agent/src/policy/mod.rs`: add the two modules and re-exports.

**Defaults:** PIN `min_length` 6, `max_length` 127, `digits` required, other classes allowed, `history` 0, no expiry, `lockout_attempts` 5, `lockout_minutes` 15. Methods: `biometrics_allowed` true, `face_requires_ir` true, `require_hardware_tpm` true. Every context (`login`, `unlock`, `sudo`, `session`): methods pin, fingerprint, face; factors 1; no `reverify_after`. No relying-party classes.

**More restrictive is:** larger `min_length`, `history`, `lockout_minutes`, `factors`; smaller `max_length`, `expiry_days`, `lockout_attempts`, `reverify_after` (absent is least restrictive); `required` or `disallowed` beats `allowed`, and `required` against `disallowed` is a contradiction; `biometrics_allowed` false; `face_requires_ir`, `require_hardware_tpm`, `require_second_credential` true; `methods` intersection; provider `tpm` > `keepassxc` > `any`; prompt `reverify` > `presence` > `none`; `match` for the same class name: union.

**Layering:** (1) merge all admin layers, most restrictive per key; (2) per key: admin value if set (managed), else most restrictive of default and user (the user can tighten, never loosen); (3) invariants: add `pin` to every context's methods; if `biometrics_allowed` is false remove `fingerprint` and `face` everywhere; keep `factors` as merged. Return `Contradiction` if merged `max_length` < `min_length` or a class is both required and disallowed.

**Tests first** (in `merge.rs`):
- `user_can_tighten_a_default`, `user_cannot_loosen_a_default`
- `user_cannot_override_admin_setting` (admin loosens `min_length` to 4, user sets 8: effective 4, managed)
- `conflicting_admin_files_resolve_to_most_restrictive` (one case per key family)
- `contradictory_merge_is_reported`
- `pin_is_always_allowed` (admin sets `methods = ["face"]` for `sudo`)
- `biometrics_disabled_leaves_only_pin`

**Constraints:**
- Invariant 3, fail closed: "Unparseable policy denies everything except the PIN. No fallback silently weakens authentication."
- Invariant 4: no `unsafe`. The crate root keeps `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.
- Invariant 8: no host names, home paths or machine details in code, tests or commits.
- Dependencies: only those named in this brief. No `unwrap()`/`expect()` outside tests.

**Acceptance:**
```sh
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
cargo deny check
bash scripts/ci/unsafe-policy.sh
```

**Out of scope:** reading files, the PIN-only state, queries. Do not change `schema.rs` except to derive `Clone`/`PartialEq` if needed.

title: Policy 3/4: load policy files from disk, failing closed
body:
Depends on Policy 2/4.

## Implementation brief

**Goal:** `load(admin_dir: &Path, user_file: &Path, admin_owner_uid: u32) -> Policy` never fails: it returns the effective policy, or the PIN-only state with a reason.

**Files:**
1. `crates/linuxhello-agent/src/policy/load.rs` (new): reading, checks, PIN-only state, tests.
2. `crates/linuxhello-agent/src/policy/mod.rs`: the `Policy` type (effective policy or PIN-only with a `reason: String`) and re-exports.
3. `crates/linuxhello-agent/Cargo.toml`: add `tempfile = "3.27.0"` under `[dev-dependencies]`.

**Rules:**
- Admin files: every `*.toml` directly in `admin_dir`, read in name order. A missing `admin_dir` or `user_file` contributes nothing.
- PIN-only state if: any file exists but cannot be read, is not UTF-8 or fails `parse_layer`; `admin_dir` or an admin file is not owned by `admin_owner_uid` or has the group- or other-write bit set (`std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt`, `PermissionsExt`); `merge` returns a contradiction.
- PIN-only state means: every context allows only `pin` with factors 1; PIN rules are the defaults; every relying party gets provider `tpm`, prompt `reverify`, factors 1.
- Production passes `admin_owner_uid = 0`; tests pass the current user's uid so they run without root.

**Tests first** (in `load.rs`, using `tempfile::TempDir`):
- `missing_files_use_defaults`
- `unparseable_user_file_leaves_only_pin`, `unparseable_admin_file_leaves_only_pin`
- `non_utf8_file_leaves_only_pin`
- `admin_file_writable_by_others_leaves_only_pin` (chmod 0o666), `admin_file_with_wrong_owner_leaves_only_pin` (pass a uid that is not the file's)
- `contradictory_merge_leaves_only_pin`
- `pin_only_state_requires_tpm_and_reverify`
- `pin_only_reason_names_the_file` (the reason contains the offending file name, not its content)

**Constraints:**
- Invariant 3, fail closed: "Unparseable policy denies everything except the PIN. No fallback silently weakens authentication."
- Invariant 4: no `unsafe`. The crate root keeps `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.
- Invariant 8: no host names, home paths or machine details in code, tests or commits.
- Dependencies: only those named in this brief. No `unwrap()`/`expect()` outside tests.
- Never log or return file contents in the reason: a policy file may be malformed on purpose.

**Acceptance:**
```sh
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
cargo deny check
bash scripts/ci/unsafe-policy.sh
```

**Out of scope:** watching files for changes, D-Bus, queries.

title: Policy 4/4: policy queries for contexts and relying parties
body:
Depends on Policy 3/4.

## Implementation brief

**Goal:** answer the engine's queries from a loaded `Policy`.

**Files:**
1. `crates/linuxhello-agent/src/policy/query.rs` (new): queries and tests.
2. `crates/linuxhello-agent/src/policy/mod.rs`: re-exports.

**Queries:**
- `methods_for(&self, context: Context) -> MethodRule` (methods, factors, `reverify_after`).
- `decision_for(&self, rp_id: &str) -> RpDecision` (provider, prompt, factors, `require_second_credential`). Normalise `rp_id`: lower-case, strip one trailing dot. An exact pattern matches only that domain. `*.d` matches any name ending in `.d` with at least one label before it, never `d` itself and never `xd` (e.g. `*.bank.example` does not match `evilbank.example`). The most specific match wins: exact beats wildcard, longer suffix beats shorter; ties merge most restrictive. No match: provider `any`, prompt `presence`, factors 1, no second credential. In the PIN-only state: provider `tpm`, prompt `reverify`, factors 1.
- `pin_rules(&self) -> PinRules`.
